title: Drunken driving and the 2019 penalty amendment — Motor Vehicles Act 1988 s.185

review.method: Encoded from the text of s.185 as amended by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019. Deliberately small: the point is to show that the same analysis runs on a statute that is not a penal code, and that a purely monetary amendment can be measured.

in_scope: the alcohol limb (30 mg per 100 ml)
out_of_scope: s.203-204 breath and laboratory testing procedure

sources.note: Raised the first-offence fine from Rs 2,000 to Rs 10,000 and the subsequent-offence fine from Rs 3,000 to Rs 15,000. Custodial ceilings unchanged.

This note still describes the enhanced penalty as applying to a second offence 'within three years'. The words of the sub-section as amended in 2019 contain no such window. The disagreement is recorded as an ambiguity rather than resolved.

facts.name: was_driving
facts.label: Driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle on a public place

facts.name: blood_alcohol_mg
facts.label: Blood alcohol, mg per 100 ml (30 is the statutory threshold)

facts.name: incapable_due_to_drug
facts.label: Under the influence of a drug to the extent of being incapable of exercising proper control

value_labels.more_than_three_years: one, more than three years ago

terms.definition: Once blood alcohol exceeds 30 mg per 100 ml the offence is complete; there is no separate need to prove bad driving.

branches.text: Whoever, while driving, or attempting to drive, a motor vehicle ...
branches.notes: Sleeping in a parked car, or driving on private land outside the Act's public-place requirement, falls outside s.185.

branches.text: has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser, or in any other test including a laboratory test
branches.notes: Strictly 'exceeding': exactly 30 mg is not an offence. The threshold is a parameter so an amendment to it can be measured.

branches.text: is under the influence of a drug to such an extent as to be incapable of exercising proper control over the vehicle
Below the statutory threshold and not incapacitated: the conduct described in s.185 is not made out.
branches.notes: Explicit fall-through. Without it the analyser would report lawful driving as a gap in the rules, which it is not.

punishment_rules.text: Second or subsequent offence: imprisonment up to 24 months, or fine of Rs 15,000, or both [s.185, post-2019]
Second or subsequent offence within three years: imprisonment up to 24 months, or fine of Rs 15,000, or both [s.185, three-year window reading]
First offence: imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine of Rs 10,000, or both [s.185, post-2019]

ambiguities.question: Does the enhanced penalty for a 'second or subsequent offence' require the earlier conviction to be within three years?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: If a window applies, an offender convicted four years ago is sentenced under the first-offence tariff (Rs 10,000, up to 6 months). If not, the enhanced tariff (Rs 15,000, up to 24 months) applies for life. Same facts, different sentence and different maximum custody.
ambiguities.position_a: No window: the 2019 amendment removed the limiting words; the enhanced penalty applies to any second offence.
ambiguities.position_b: Three-year window: the enhanced penalty applies only to an offence committed within three years of the previous similar offence.

variants.label: no window (current encoding, parameter is null)

illustrations.text: A reading of exactly 30 mg per 100 ml does not exceed 30 mg, so the per se limb is not made out.
A reading of 31 mg exceeds the threshold and completes the offence.
The drug limb has no numeric threshold: incapacity is the test.
Intoxication alone is not an offence; the section requires driving or attempting to drive.
